lines.author: ai
lines.content: The Utility Line Assignment (ULA) application process is the procedure by which a Designer determines whether a ULA permit is required, completes a ULA application drawing and form, circulates the application to stakeholders, and finalizes and files the permit once conditions are resolved. It is a City of Edmonton requirement for installing utility assets within the road allowance where ground disturbance is required. The process map trigger is 'Prepare ULA Document', and the application is submitted at https://ula.edmonton.ca.

lines.author: ai
lines.content: The 3.1 ULA application process is documented as a City of Edmonton flowchart with lanes for the Designer, Drafting Tech, City of Edmonton, Stakeholders, and Data. In the process map, the marker (A) indicates a required coordination between drafting and design to ensure the drawing meets designer requirements. The Data lane contains Microstation EO entries and Outlook, Adobe, and the COE ULA Website.

lines.author: ai
lines.content:
The process then proceeds as follows:
1. The Designer completes the preliminary design, an initial design completed before investigating whether a ULA is required, then determines whether a ULA permit is required and notifies the Drafting Technologist when one is.
2. The Drafting Technologist completes the design and ULA application drawings according to EPCOR's construction drawing standard.
3. The Designer reviews the ULA application drawing for accuracy; if it is inaccurate, the Designer marks all corrections on the drawing and sends it back to the Drafting Technologist for modifications.
4. The Designer completes the ULA application form online and attaches all required documents, such as the ULA drawing in PDF format.
5. The City of Edmonton Transportation Office acknowledges receipt of the online application, provides the contact person's name and the process time frame, and circulates the proposed design to all Stakeholders.

lines.author: ai
lines.content:
Circulation and stakeholder review follow:
6. Each Stakeholder reviews and comments on the proposed design circulated by the Transportation Office, and may comment via e-mail or phone call; if a Stakeholder finds no issues or conflicts, the proposed design is approved and the process proceeds to step 8.0.
7. In step 8.0, the Stakeholder approves the proposed facility locations with comments and sends them to the City of Edmonton Transportation Department.
8. A Stakeholder may instead respond to the circulation with conflicts to the City of Edmonton, and the COE will advise the Designer of the conflicts or objections; if a Stakeholder identifies conflicts with the proposed design, the process proceeds to step 6.0, Reply to circulation with objections, where stakeholders reply with objections where applicable and work with the Designer to resolve conditions before the design is finalized and the ULA permit is filed.
9. The City of Edmonton processes the application, approves the ULA application and the proposed facility locations, and issues a ULA permit number in step 9.0.

lines.author: ai
lines.content:
Permit receipt and closing steps follow:
10. The Designer receives the ULA permit from the City of Edmonton and reviews it; if there are any conditions the process goes to step 11, and if there are no conditions it proceeds to step 12.
11. Stakeholder conditions, which arise during the ULA application process, are handled in step 11.0: the Designer goes back to the Stakeholders to discuss or clarify the permit conditions and must resolve or clarify the issue and mutually agree to the resolution with the Stakeholders; if necessary, the drawing may need to be modified and resubmitted.
12. In step 12.0, the Designer adds the ULA permit number to the design drawing and work order, and includes the ULA permit, Stakeholder comments, and Stakeholder drawings if applicable in the work order package.
13. A scanned copy of all the ULA documents is added to the project file.

lines.author: ai
lines.content: The ULA application form is the form the Designer completes online as part of the process, after confirming the drawing is accurate; according to its description, if the drawing is not accurate the Designer sends a resolution to the City of Edmonton instead. The ULA permit is the permit the Designer receives after submitting the form, and the Designer must resolve any stakeholder conditions, then finalize the design and file the ULA permit to complete the application.
